chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Freddie Keppard: loud ragtime trumpet and the Orpheum circuit
summary: Danny and Milt recall Keppard's loud, ragged style and his decade on the Orpheum circuit with the Original Dixieland band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Freddie Keppard was fantastic. You heard Freddie.
Well, Freddie was a Ragtime trumpet player. Am I right?
He seemed like he played ragged.
But he was strong, boy. He was so loud, man. Whoo!
Yeah, he would blast the horn. Well, the people would look at him, right.
Yeah, whoa. I played with him at 35th and State Street, up there where that Jesse Benga bank was. Do you remember that bank in those days?

Oh, he was fabulous, man. He lived on up by the Vincennes Hotel, 36th and Vincennes over there. I think that's where he died. Because he was getting... He was sick when I was playing, because he was on...you know, he was on

Well, he had been on the Orpheum circuit for about ten years, from about 1909, the year I was born, until, what, 1918 or 1919, when the Dixieland Band recorded... Them people had been on the Orpheum circuit, him and Big-Eye Louis, a band from New Orleans...
